headings: Papzimeos (zopapogene imadenovec-drba, PRGN-2012) - Our FDA Approved Commercial Product
paragraphs: We are a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company specializing in the advancement of innovative precision medicines to improve the lives of patients. We are leveraging our proprietary technology platforms to develop product candidates designed to target urgent and intractable diseases in our core therapeutic areas of immuno-oncology, autoimmune disorders, and infectious diseases.

We believe that our array of technology platforms uniquely positions us among other biotechnology companies to advance precision medicine. Precision medicine is the practice of therapeutic product development that takes into account specific genetic variations within populations impacted by a disease to design targeted therapies to improve outcomes for a disease or patient population. Our proprietary and complementary technology platforms provide a strong foundation to realize the core promise of precision medicine by supporting our efforts to construct powerful gene programs to drive efficacy, deliver these programs through viral, non-viral, and microbe-based approaches to drive lower costs, and control gene expression to drive safety. Our therapeutic platforms, including AdenoVerse immunotherapy, and UltraCAR-T, are designed to allow us to precisely control the level and physiological location of gene expression and modify biological molecules to control the function and output of living cells to treat underlying disease conditions. We have developed a proprietary electroporation device, UltraPorator, designed to further streamline and ensure the rapid and cost-effective manufacturing of UltraCAR-T therapies.

In August 2025, the FDA granted full approval to our product, Papzimeos (zopapogene imadenovec-drba, PRGN-2012), for the treatment of adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP). RRP is a rare, debilitating, and potentially life-threatening disease caused by chronic human papillomavirus (HPV) 6 or HPV 11 infection, which results in recurrent benign tumors in the respiratory tract. Papzimeos is a non-replicating adenoviral vector-based immunotherapy designed to express a fusion antigen comprising selected regions of HPV types 6 and 11 proteins. Papzimeos is designed to generate an immune response directed against HPV 6 and HPV 11 proteins in patients with RRP.

Our clinical pipeline includes PRGN-2009, which is based on our AdenoVerse immunotherapy platform; and PRGN-3005, PRGN-3006 and PRGN-3007, which are built on our UltraCAR-T platform. We have completed enrollment in the Phase 1b clinical trial of PRGN-3006. As part of the strategic prioritization of our pipeline we announced in August 2024 that we have paused enrollment in the PRGN-3005 and PRGN-3007 clinical trials. In addition, we announced a plan to continue PRGN-2009 Phase 2 clinical trials under a cooperative research and development agreement ("CRADA") with the National Cancer Institute ("NCI") in recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer and in newly diagnosed HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer.

We exercise discipline in our portfolio management by systematically evaluating data from our preclinical programs in order to make rapid "go" and "no go" decisions. Through this process, we believe we can more effectively allocate resources to programs that we believe show the most promise and advance such programs to clinical trials.
To guide our decision-making and operations, we have adopted the following tenets, which form the core of our operating ideology:
•Financial Discipline. Responsibly allocate capital in an effort to ensure maximum value creation.
•Active Portfolio Management. Continuously evaluate our portfolio and strictly adhere to data-driven "go" and "no go" decisions to advance programs with the highest probability of success.
•Rapid Execution. Advance priority programs quickly to value inflection points.
•Strategic Partnerships. Seek strategic partnerships to maximize value generation.

Our strategy is to use our discovery and clinical development infrastructure to continue advancement of our clinical programs with the goal of improving outcomes for patients with significant unmet medical needs. The key elements of our strategy include:
•Advancing our lead clinical stage programs and seeking opportunities to maximize their value. We are actively

advancing our lead programs that we believe have significant potential value. We intend to efficiently pursue these programs toward clinical proof-of-concept and commercialization, whether independently or with collaborators.

•Strategically pursuing our preclinical programs. We are strategically focusing on selecting preclinical programs to create long-term value. Through this process, we believe we can more effectively allocate resources to programs that we believe show the most promise and advance such programs to clinical trials.

headings: Risks Related to Our Financial Position and Capital Needs
We are substantially dependent on the commercial success of Papzimeos
We have a history of net losses, and we may not achieve or maintain profitability.
We expect our future capital requirements will be substantial and will depend on many factors.
Our level of indebtedness and debt service obligations could adversely affect our financial condition and may make it more difficult for us to fund our operations.
Failure of the U.S. federal government to manage its fiscal matters or to raise or further suspend the debt ceiling may expose us to increased financial and operational risk.
Risks Related to the Discovery and Development of Our Product Candidates
The market opportunities for our product and product candidates may be smaller than we estimate.
We may find it difficult to enroll patients in clinical trials, which could delay or prevent us from proceeding with clinical trials.
We may be required to suspend, repeat, or terminate our clinical trials if they are not conducted in accordance with regulatory requirements, or the trials are not well designed.
Papzimeos and our product candidates are novel, complex, and difficult to manufacture.
Risks Related to the Commercialization of our Product and Product Candidates and Other Legal Compliance Matters

Our product and product candidates may fail to achieve the degree of market acceptance by physicians, patients, third-party payers, and others in the medical community necessary for commercial success.
Delays in obtaining regulatory approval of manufacturing processes and facilities or disruptions in manufacturing processes may delay or disrupt our commercialization efforts.

To date, we have invested substantial efforts and financial resources in the research, development and commercialization of Papzimeos and our product candidates. Our near-term prospects, including our ability to develop our product candidates and generate revenue, and our future growth are substantially dependent on the commercial success of Papzimeos. Although we received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, we are pursing regulatory approval from the European Commission, and are preparing to file for approval from other foreign regulatory bodies, for Papzimeos for the treatment of RRP in adults, we can provide no assurances that we will obtain regulatory approval in any jurisdiction other than the U.S., which could have an adverse impact on our results of operations. In addition, the successful commercialization of Papzimeos will depend on a number of factors and involves risk, including some of the risks identified in these "Risk Factors." One or
more of these risks, many of which are beyond our control, could cause significant delays or an inability to successfully commercialize Papzimeos.

We have incurred net losses since our inception, with the exception of 2022 where we had $28.3 million in net income due to the sale of TransOva, which generated a gain on divestiture of $94.7 million. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $2.3 billion. We expect to incur losses and negative cash flows from operating activities for the foreseeable future.

On August 14, 2025, we received FDA approval for Papzimeos for adults with RRP. We anticipate that our expenses will increase substantially as we commercialize Papzimeos, continue to advance the preclinical and clinical development of our existing product candidates and continue our research activities, and there is a significant risk that our product candidates will fail to demonstrate adequate efficacy or an acceptable safety profile, obtain regulatory approval, or become commercially viable. As we commercialize Papzimeos and if we obtain regulatory approval of Papzimeos in other jurisdictions or indications or for our other product candidates, we expect we will incur significant commercialization expenses related to product sales, marketing, manufacturing and distribution. We have and are devoting substantial resources to the commercial infrastructure for Papzimeos and have not yet achieved significant product revenue. A significant period of time could pass before Papzimeos generates significant product revenue, or commercialization of our various product candidates or before the execution of contractual relationships providing for up-front payments, milestones or royalties sufficient to achieve profitability. As a result, our expenses may exceed revenues for the foreseeable future, and we may not achieve profitability. If we fail to achieve profitability, or if the time required to achieve profitability is longer than we anticipate, we may not be able to continue our business. Even if we do achieve profitability, we may not be able to sustain or increase profitability on a quarterly or annual basis.

We are a biopharmaceutical company specializing in the advancement of innovative precision medicines to address difficult-to-treat diseases with high unmet patient need. Precigen is dedicated to advancing scientific breakthroughs from proof-of-concept through commercialization. We are leveraging our proprietary technology platforms to develop product candidates designed to target urgent and intractable diseases in our core therapeutic areas of immuno-oncology, autoimmune disorders, and infectious diseases.

We believe that our array of technology platforms uniquely positions us among other biotechnology companies to advance precision medicine. Our proprietary and complementary technology platforms provide a strong foundation to realize the core promise of precision medicine by supporting our efforts to construct powerful gene programs to drive efficacy, deliver these programs through viral, non-viral, and microbe-based approaches to drive lower costs, and control gene expression to drive safety. Our therapeutic platforms, including AdenoVerse immunotherapy, UltraCAR-T, and ActoBiotics, are designed to allow us to precisely control the level and physiological location of gene expression and modify biological molecules to control the function and output of living cells to treat underlying disease conditions. We have developed a proprietary electroporation device, UltraPorator, designed to further streamline and ensure the rapid and cost-effective manufacturing of UltraCAR-T therapies.

Our commercial product, Papzimeos (zopapogene imadenovec-drba, PRGN-2012), is the first and only US Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") approved therapy for the treatment of adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis ("RRP"). Papzimeos is a non-replicating adenoviral vector-based immunotherapy designed to express a fusion antigen comprising selected regions of human papillomavirus (HPV) types 6 and 11 proteins. Papzimeos is designed to generate an immune response directed against HPV 6 and HPV 11 proteins in patients with RRP. Discovered and designed in Precigen's labs using Precigen's proprietary AdenoVerse therapeutic platform, Papzimeos represents a new therapeutic paradigm for RRP.

Our clinical pipeline includes PRGN-2009, which are based on our AdenoVerse immunotherapy platform; and PRGN-3005, PRGN-3006 and PRGN-3007, which are built on our UltraCAR-T platform. We have completed enrollment in the Phase 1b clinical trial of PRGN-3006. As part of the strategic prioritization of our pipeline announced in August 2024, we paused enrollment in the PRGN-3005 and PRGN-3007 clinical trials, minimized UltraCAR-T spending and plan to focus on strategic

partnerships to further advance UltraCAR-T programs. In addition, we previously announced plans to continue PRGN-2009 Phase 2 clinical trials under a cooperative research and development agreement ("CRADA") with the National Cancer Institute ("NCI") in recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer and in newly diagnosed HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer.

In August 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") granted full approval of Papzimeos for the treatment of adults with RRP. RRP is a rare, debilitating, and potentially life-threatening disease caused by chronic human papillomavirus ("HPV") 6 or HPV 11 infection, which results in recurrent benign tumors in the respiratory tract. RRP can lead to severe voice disturbance, a compromised airway, and recurrent post-obstructive pneumonias. Management of RRP has primarily consisted of repeated surgeries, which do not address the root cause of the disease and can be associated with significant morbidity as well as significant patient and health system burden. The approval of Papzimeos marks a historic milestone for the RRP patient community as the first and only FDA-approved therapy for the treatment of adults with RRP. As a result of Papzimeos receiving full FDA approval, a confirmatory clinical trial is not required.

Papzimeos is a non-replicating adenoviral vector-based immunotherapy designed to express a fusion antigen comprising selected regions of HPV types 6 and 11 proteins—the root cause of RRP. Papzimeos is delivered via four subcutaneous injections over a 12-week interval. Papzimeos approval is supported by safety and efficacy data from the pivotal Phase 1/2 clinical trial published in the Lancet Respiratory Medicine. The pivotal study successfully met its primary safety and pre-specified primary efficacy endpoints. Papzimeos was well-tolerated with no dose-limiting toxicities and no treatment-related adverse events greater than Grade 2. Of the patients in our study, 51% (18 out of 35) achieved complete response, requiring no surgeries in the 12 months after treatment with Papzimeos. These complete responses have been durable after Papzimeos treatment with median follow-up of 36 months as of a September 19, 2025 data cutoff.

Exemplar generates product and service revenues through the development and sale of genetically engineered miniature swine models. We recognize revenue when control of the promised product or service is transferred to the customer. In 2025, revenues generated by Exemplar became less significant to the Company, and we expect this significance to greatly diminish into the future.

During the fourth quarter of 2025, we began generating revenue from commercial sales of Papzimeos, our FDA‑approved immunotherapy for RRP. While revenues from Papzimeos were limited in the year due to the timing of our commercial launch, we anticipate our future revenue to primarily be generated from Papzimeos product sales.

As we transition to a commercial‑stage company, our future revenues will increasingly depend on our ability to successfully commercialize Papzimeos, advance our proprietary programs, and bring additional products enabled by our technology platforms to market.

We anticipate that collaboration revenue will remain minimal in the near term, except in cases of future strategic transactions involving our platforms or programs. Should new collaboration agreements or strategic transactions be executed, revenue could be positively impacted.
Accordingly, there can be no assurance as to the timing, magnitude, and predictability of revenues, if any, to which we might be entitled.

paragraphs: 本公司為一家商業階段的生物科技公司，專門從事創新精準醫療藥物的發展，以改善病患的生活品質。本公司運用自有專利技術平台，開發產品候選藥物，用以針對免疫腫瘤學、自身免疫性疾病及感染性疾病等核心治療領域中，亟需且難以治療的疾病。

本公司認為，我們的技術平台組合使我們在其他生物科技公司中獨樹一幟，能有效推動精準醫療的發展。精準醫療是透過考量特定疾病族羣中的遺傳變異，設計針對性療法以改善疾病或特定族羣的治療結果。我們的自有且互補技術平台，為實現精準醫療的核心承諾提供了強固基礎，支持我們構建強大基因程式以提升療效、透過病毒、非病毒及微生物基質方式傳遞這些程式以降低製造成本，並控制基因表現以提升安全性。我們的治療平台，包括 AdenoVerse 免疫療法及 UltraCAR-T，設計用以讓我們能精確控制基因表現的層級與生理位置，並修改生物分子以控制活細胞的功能與輸出，用以治療基礎疾病。

2025 年 8 月，美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）已核准本公司產品 Papzimeos（zopapogene imadenovec-drba, PRGN-2012）用於治療成人反覆性呼吸道乳頭瘤病（RRP）。RRP 是一種罕見、使人無法正常生活且可能威脅生命的疾病，由慢性人乳頭瘤病毒（HPV）6 或 HPV 11 感染引起，導致呼吸道反覆出現良性腫瘤。Papzimeos 是一種非複製性腺病毒載體基質的免疫療法，設計用以表現包含 HPV 6 與 HPV 11 蛋白質選取區域的融合抗原。Papzimeos 設計用以在 RRP 患者中產生針對 HPV 6 與 HPV 11 蛋白質的免疫反應。

我們的臨牀產品線包括基於 AdenoVerse 免疫療法平台的 PRGN-2009，以及基於 UltraCAR-T 平台的 PRGN-3005、PRGN-3006 與 PRGN-3007。我們已完成 PRGN-3006 的 Phase 1b 臨牀試驗入組。根據我們在 2024 年 8 月宣佈的策略性產品線優先順序，我們已暫停 PRGN-3005 與 PRGN-3007 的臨牀試驗入組。此外，我們也宣佈計畫在與國家癌症研究所（NCI）簽訂的合作研究與發展協議（CRADA）下，繼續進行 PRGN-2009 的 Phase 2 臨牀試驗，用於治療復發/轉移性子宮頸癌及新診斷的 HPV 相關口咽癌。
我們在產品組合管理上保持嚴謹，透過系統性評估預臨牀計畫的數據，以快速做出「進行」與「停止」的決策。透過此過程，我們相信能更有效地將資源配置至我們認為最有潛力的計畫，並推動這些計畫進入臨牀試驗。
為引導我們的決策與營運，我們採納以下原則，這些原則構成我們營運理念的核心：
•財務紀律。負責任地配置資金，以確保最大價值創造。
•主動產品組合管理。持續評估我們的產品組合，並嚴格遵循數據驅動的「進行」與「停止」決策，以推動成功機率最高的計畫。
•快速執行。優先推動高價值轉折點的計畫。
•戰略合作夥伴。尋求戰略合作夥伴以最大化價值創造。
我們的策略是利用我們的發現與臨牀開發基礎設施，持續推進我們的臨牀計畫，目標為改善有重大未滿足醫療需求病患的治療結果。我們策略的關鍵要素包括：
•推進我們的領先臨牀階段計畫，並尋求機會最大化其價值。我們積極
推進我們認為具有顯著潛在價值的領先計畫。我們意圖高效地推動這些計畫朝向臨牀概念驗證與商業化，無論是獨立進行或與合作夥伴共同進行。
•戰略性地追求我們的前期臨牀計畫。我們戰略性地聚焦於選擇前期臨牀計畫以創造長期價值。我們在組合管理上保持嚴謹，透過系統性評估前期臨牀計畫的數據，以快速做出 "進行" 或 "中止" 的決策。透過此過程，我們相信能夠更有效地將資源分配至我們認為最有潛力的計畫，並推動這些計畫進入臨牀試驗。

本公司為專門從事創新精準醫療藥物研發之生物科技公司，致力於解決高未滿足醫療需求之難治性疾病。Precigen 致力於從概念驗證階段至商業化之科學突破。我們正運用自有專利技術平台，開發針對緊急且難治性疾病之產品候選藥物，專注於免疫腫瘤學、自身免疫性疾病及感染性疾病等核心治療領域。

我們相信，我們的技術平台組合使我們在其他生物科技公司中獨樹一幟，能推動精準醫療的發展。我們的自有且補充性技術平台，為實現精準醫療的核心承諾提供了強大基礎，支持我們構建強大基因程式以提高療效、透過病毒、非病毒及微生物基質方式遞送這些程式以降低成本，並控制基因表達以提高安全性。我們的治療平台，包括 AdenoVerse 免疫療法、UltraCAR-T 及 ActoBiotics，設計用以讓我們精確控制基因表達的層級與生理位置，並修改生物分子以控制活細胞的功能與輸出，以治療基礎疾病。我們已開發出自有專利電穿孔裝置 UltraPorator，設計用以進一步簡化並確保 UltraCAR-T 療法的快速且成本效益高的製造。

我們的商業產品 Papzimeos（zopapogene imadenovec-drba, PRGN-2012），為美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）批准的首個且唯一用於治療成人反覆性呼吸道乳頭瘤病（"RRP"）的療法。Papzimeos 為一種非複製性腺病毒載體基質免疫療法，設計用以表達包含人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV）6 與 11 蛋白質選定區域之融合抗原。Papzimeos 設計用以在 RRP 患者中產生針對 HPV 6 與 HPV 11 蛋白質之免疫反應。Papzimeos 在 Precigen 實驗室中，運用 Precigen 自有專利 AdenoVerse 治療平台發現並設計，代表 RRP 之新治療模式。

我們的臨牀產品線包括 PRGN-2009，基於我們 AdenoVerse 免疫療法平台；以及 PRGN-3005、PRGN-3006 與 PRGN-3007，基於我們 UltraCAR-T 平台。我們已完成 PRGN-3006 之 Phase 1b 臨牀試驗入組。根據 2024 年 8 月宣佈的產品線戰略優先順序，我們已暫停 PRGN-3005 與 PRGN-3007 臨牀試驗入組，減少 UltraCAR-T 費用，並計畫專注於戰略
合作夥伴以進一步推動 UltraCAR-T 計畫。此外，我們先前宣佈計畫在與國家癌症研究所（"NCI"）簽訂的合作研究與發展協議（"CRADA"）下，繼續 PRGN-2009 之 Phase 2 臨牀試驗，用於治療反覆性/轉移性子宮頸癌及新診斷之 HPV 相關口咽癌。

2025 年 8 月，美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）批准 Papzimeos 用於治療成人 RRP。RRP 為一種罕見、使人衰弱且可能危及生命的疾病，由慢性人類乳頭瘤病毒（"HPV"）6 或 HPV 11 感染引起，導致呼吸道反覆良性腫瘤。RRP 可導致嚴重聲音障礙、氣道受損及反覆性氣道阻塞肺炎。RRP 的管理主要為反覆手術，但無法解決疾病的根本原因，且可能伴隨顯著的併發症及患者與醫療系統的負擔。Papzimeos 的批准為 RRP 患者社羣帶來歷史性里程碑，為首個且唯一 FDA 批准用於治療成人 RRP 的療法。由於 Papzimeos 獲得完整 FDA 批准，因此無需進行確認性臨牀試驗。

Papzimeos 為一種非複製性腺病毒載體基質免疫療法，設計用以表達包含 HPV 6 與 11 蛋白質選定區域之融合抗原——RRP 的根本原因。Papzimeos 透過四次皮下注射，在 12 週間間隔施打。Papzimeos 的批准獲得了來自《Lancet Respiratory Medicine》發表的關鍵 Phase 1/2 臨牀試驗之安全性與有效性數據支持。關鍵研究成功達成其主要安全性與預設主要有效性終點。Papzimeos 被認為耐受性良好，無劑量限制性毒性，且無與治療相關的不良事件高於 Grade 2。在我們的試驗中，51%（18 名 / 35 名）患者在施打 Papzimeos 後 12 個月內無需手術，達成完全反應。這些完全反應在 Papzimeos 治療後持續，截至 2025 年 9 月 19 日數據截止日，中位數追蹤時間為 36 個月。
請參閱第 7 項「流動性及資本資源」部分下方關於 2025 年融資交易的進一步討論。
Exemplar 透過開發及銷售基因工程微型豬模型產生產品及服務收入。我們在將承諾的產品或服務的控制權轉移給客戶時確認收入。2025 年，Exemplar 所產生的收入對本公司而言變得較不重要，我們預期此重要性將在未來大幅降低。
在 2025 年第四季，我們開始從 Papzimeos 的商業銷售中產生收入，Papzimeos 是我們獲得 FDA 批准的 RRP 免疫治療藥物。雖然由於商業發佈的時程，Papzimeos 在該年度產生的收入有限，但我們預期未來收入將主要來自 Papzimeos 產品的銷售。
隨著我們轉型為商業階段公司，未來收入將越來越依賴我們成功商業化 Papzimeos、推進我們的專有計畫，以及將更多由我們技術平台啟動的產品推向市場的能力。
我們預期在近期內，合作收入將保持為少量，除非未來有涉及我們平台或計畫的戰略交易。若未來簽訂新的合作協議或戰略交易，收入可能會受到正面影響。
因此，無法保證我們可能有權獲得的收入的時間、規模及可預測性，如有任何收入的話。

截至目前為止，我們已投入大量努力與財務資源於 Papzimeos 的研究、開發與商業化，以及我們的產品候選藥物。我們近期的前景，包括我們開發產品候選藥物與產生收入的能力，以及我們未來的成長，很大程度上取決於 Papzimeos 的商業成功。雖然我們已獲得美國食品藥物管理局，或 FDA 的批准，我們正在追求歐洲委員會的監管批准，並準備向其他外國監管機構提交批准申請，以用於治療成人 RRP 的 Papzimeos，我們無法保證我們會在任何除美國以外的司法管轄區獲得監管批准，這可能會對我們的營運結果造成不利影響。此外，Papzimeos 的成功商業化將取決於許多因素，並涉及風險，包括這些「風險因素」中所識別的一些風險。一個或
更多這些風險，許多是超出我們控制範圍，可能會導致重大延誤或無法成功商業化 Papzimeos。
自我們成立以來，我們已產生淨虧損，除了 2022 年，當時我們因出售 TransOva 而取得 28.3 百萬美元淨收入，該交易產生 94.7 百萬美元處分收益。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們累積虧損為 2.3 十億美元。我們預期在可預見的未來，將產生虧損及來自營運活動的負面現金流。

2025 年 8 月 14 日，我們獲得美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准 Papzimeos 用於成人 RRP 患者。我們預期在商業化 Papzimeos、持續推進現有產品候選藥物的臨牀前及臨牀開發，並持續進行研究活動時，費用將大幅增加，且有顯著風險，即我們的產品候選藥物可能無法顯示足夠的療效或可接受的安全性，取得監管核准，或成為商業可行的產品。在商業化 Papzimeos 並在其他司法管轄區或適應症或我們其他產品候選藥物取得監管核准的情況下，我們預期將產生與產品銷售、行銷、製造及分銷相關的重大商業化費用。我們已投入大量資源建立 Papzimeos 的商業基礎設施，但尚未取得顯著的產品收入。一段相當長的時間可能經過，Pazimeos 才能產生顯著的產品收入，或商業化我們各種產品候選藥物，或在執行提供 upfront 支付、里程碑或版稅的契約關係，以達到獲利能力。因此，我們的費用可能超過收入，且在可預見的未來，我們可能無法實現獲利。如果我們無法實現獲利，或實現獲利所需時間長於我們預期，我們可能無法繼續經營業務。即使我們實現獲利，我們也可能無法維持或提高季度或年度的獲利能力。
